subject: SSE tail latency spike impacting Wavefront Health during evening peak

From: Elena Vasquez <elena@wavefront.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Wavefront] Evening SSE tail latency spike causing drops

Hi Priya —

We're seeing a recurring issue this week between ~18:00-20:00 PT where our users on the Wavefront webchat see message delivery delays and occasional dropped messages. The worst impact is tail latency (p99) on your hosted SSE endpoint. Attached is a heatmap from our monitoring and a short trace showing a bunch of 502/504s from the upstream (your endpoint).

High-level metrics from tonight: p95 ~420ms -> 1.1s, p99 spikes to 5.3s, connection churn +12% vs baseline, 502s peaking at 0.9% of requests in the window. This is blocking our evening traffic and affecting session continuity for customers.

Can you confirm you received the traces and advise next steps? We need an ETA for mitigation — our CS team is getting pressure from product and ops.

Thanks,
Elena
Platform Eng, Wavefront Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 18:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Wavefront] Evening SSE tail latency spike causing drops

Thanks Priya / Elena. I pulled the traces Elena attached; preliminary look indicates a backlog forming at the edge proxies during the 18:00-19:30 PT window. Two quick observations: (1) connection accepts remain steady but response queue depth at the SSE handler increases sharply, (2) we see intermittent 502s from our route to the streaming backend (nginx upstream read timeout and HTTP2 stream resets).

I'm kicking a targeted canary to replicate at lower load and will paste a short runbook here. Possible hypotheses: kernel-level socket backlog exhaustion (under very high concurrent connections), inefficient keepalive policy interacting with our autoscaler, or a regression in the streaming runtime that increases per-connection CPU.

Immediate mitigation options (we can try in parallel):
- Increase proxy accept/backlog and upstream read timeout (quick, low risk)
- Temporarily scale Dedicated streaming pool by +20% for Wavefront (costly but immediate)
- Roll back yesterday's streaming runtime change if the canary reproduces the regression

I'll validate in the next 15 minutes and report back. Aditya, can you confirm whether we have autoscaler logs for the evening spike?

—Sean
SRE Lead
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 18:46:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Wavefront] Evening SSE tail latency spike causing drops

Got it — pulling autoscaler and host metrics now. Early read: autoscaler did increase instance count but with a 90s stabilization window; during the sharp ramp our backend queue depth kept rising faster than new replicas came online. Also seeing a slight uptick in CPU per connection on the latest streaming runtime (deploy 20280510-2).

Action I'm taking immediately:
1) Push a temporary scaling override for Wavefront to reduce stabilization window to 10s for the next 60 minutes.
2) Increase upstream read timeout on the proxy for Wavefront routes from 30s -> 60s.
3) Start a rollback job for the 20280510-2 runtime to the previous stable build if the canary shows elevated per-connection CPU.

I'll post logs for the autoscaler events and the canary results in 20 minutes.

— Aditya
Senior SRE

Elena — quick update for your ops team: we've applied a temporary scaling override and increased the proxy upstream timeout. Our canary run at 19:03 shows p99 reduced from ~5s to ~700ms and 502 rate dropped to ~0.06% in the sampled window. We're keeping monitoring in the next 2 hours and will decide whether to keep the override or perform rollback.

Marissa will follow-up on communication with your CS/Product teams; Priya from our side will coordinate any billing/credits asks if needed.

We appreciate the quick traces you provided — they were instrumental.

— Priya

Morning Elena — following up with a brief summary for Wavefront product and ops:

What we saw: evening peak produced a p99 tail spike due to backlog at proxy -> streaming runtime; linked to the 20280510-2 runtime which modestly increases per-connection CPU and interacts poorly with default autoscaler stabilization.

What we did: temporary scaling override (10s window) + upstream timeout bump. Canary showed p99 reduced to ~600-800ms, 502s reduced to baseline.

Next steps:
- SRE to roll forward a configuration change to reduce default stabilization for tiered customers during peak hours (INF-8432).
- Engineering to run a focused performance test on 20280510-2 runtime and either optimize per-connection CPU or re-release a patched build (action owner: Sean / Eng).
- Commercial: Priya to propose a goodwill credit for the impacted evening windows while we finalize a permanent fix.

I'll keep this thread open until the change is complete. If you want a short post-mortem (1 pager + timeline), we can have that by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success
